author: TEDx Talks
description:
Did you know that nearly 75% of people fear public speaking—often more than they fear death? Psychologists call it glossophobia. In this honest and inspiring talk, the speaker shares a deeply personal journey from running off stage in fear to eventually falling in love with the microphone.

From a failed self-introduction in college, to freezing during a singing competition, to finally becoming a professor and principal, this talk shows that confidence is not something you’re born with—it’s something you build through practice, discomfort, and showing up again and again.

Along the way, you’ll discover simple, practical tools to grow your stage confidence:
Start small, but start 

Prepare more than you think you should
Record yourself and improve
Aim for connection, not perfection
Keep showing up, even when you’re scared
Invest in your presence, voice, and growth

This talk is a reminder that the microphone never gets lighter—you just get stronger. If you’ve ever been afraid to speak
title: Public Speaking Confidence Isn’t Natural. It’s Built. | Dr. Swiddle D'Cunha | TEDxNMFC

author: TEDx Talks
description:
“如果我们不去认识这些千古的灭绝过程，我们就无法去抗衡未来更多的物种灭绝事件。”

动物化石，不只是冰冷的遗骸，更是解开生命谜题的钥匙。

二十多年来，林泽昇追寻跨越八千万年的痕迹，从婆罗洲亚洲象的牙齿残片，到黑风洞红毛猩猩的化石，每一次发现，都让我们更接近真相：谁在这里生活过？他们为何又消失？埋藏在化石里的答案，揭示了远古人类与环境如何一步步塑造出今日的生态面貌。

认识过去，才能守护现在。那些看似 “灭绝的故事”，其实正提醒我们：保护濒危物种，不只是科学的课题，更是你我共同的责任。

“If we fail to understand these mass extinction events from the past, we won't be able to prevent those in the future.”

More than cold and lifeless remains, fossils are the keys to unlocking the mysteries of life.

For over twenty years Lim Tze Tshen has searched for traces of history spanning 80 million years. From the tooth fragments of Bornean Asian elephants to orangutan fossils in Batu Caves, each discovery brings us closer to the truth: who once lived here? And why did they vanish? The answers buried within these fossils reveal how ancient humans and their environment have slowly but surely shaped the ecological landscape we have today.

title: 从远古生命看见未来 Seeing the Future Through Ancient Life | 林泽昇 Lim Tze Tshen | TEDxPetalingStreet

From its birth, art is given meaning and lives to give meaning to its viewers. However, beyond a first glance, it begs the question of what or who deemed it worthy of creation. Luis began his artistic journey through illustration, where his early works drew heavily from the socio-political landscape he observed during his time working at the Philippine Senate. Over the years, his practice has evolved toward a more formalist and exploratory approach, one that examines the construction and deconstruction of identity through portraiture, abstraction, and pop surrealism. His paintings and drawings reflect a continual pursuit of pushing visual language and expanding the boundaries of contemporary expression.

Elena’s journey began in medicine, but her true calling emerged in the faces of animals in need. Her work spans rescue operations, rehabilitation, and adoption for over 400 animals, as well as the leadership of life-changing and spay-neuter campaigns. Jillian Ooi unpacks the motivation behind her quest to understand and protect Malaysia’s seagrass meadows – the ways they hold underwater ecosystems together and provide our coastal communities with livelihoods. 

But they’ve been neglected through ignorance of what they are and what they do, and so she seeks out ways to make it visible, training citizen scientists to care for them through Seagrass-Watch. Drawing on her ???????-playing background, her “artscience” approach, “?????? ????” (Call of Seagrass), a series of music pieces interspersing ??????? performances with science education, has brought awareness to many since its premiere in 2023. 

As she says herself, “seagrass feeds, cleans, and fights for us. It’s time we fight for it.”

“事实能改变想法，但艺术才能真正触动人心。”

可惜的是，多年来，海草被忽视、被误解。为了让更多人 “看见” 它，黄莲心投入行动：通过 “Seagrass-Watch”（海草行动）培训公民科学家守护海草，同时结合她的甘美兰音乐背景，
title: 海底的秘密花园: 食物、家园与希望的海草故事 Seagrass Stories of Food, Home & Hope | 黄莲心 Jillian Ooi | TEDxPetalingStreet

“只要你还有心跳，你就可以去做你想做的事情。”

从懵懂的中学生，到嘻哈团体成员、酒吧老板，再到马来西亚首位 DJ 讲师，DJ Point 的人生就像一张张黑胶，不断被 Remix。

音乐，把他从一个只会弹《Zombie》的少年，带进了电音、嘻哈与教育的世界。

对他来说，DJ 不是夜店的标签，也不只是 “按 Button” 的工作。它是一门专业——要读懂音乐历史，要感受观众的情绪，要随时调控现场能量，让每一个人都能从中找到共鸣。

DJ Point 相信，音乐无界限，它能连接人群的频率，也能把梦想打进生活的节拍~

“As long as your heart is still beating, you can go after the things you dream of.”

From a curious schoolboy to hip-hop crew member, bar owner, and eventually Malaysia’s first DJ lecturer, DJ Point’s life has unfolded like a vinyl record, constantly remixed with new layers.

Music carried him from strumming ?????? as a teenager to discovering the worlds of electronic sound, hip-hop, and education.

To him, being a DJ is neither a nightclub label nor simply “pressing buttons”. It is a profession—one that calls for knowledge of music history, the ability to read the crowd, and the skill to shape energy so that every audience finds resonance.
